hypothesis: Sweep invalidated cached buffer descriptors once before subsequent descriptor preparation instead of scanning every compute state for every destroyed buffer. Live buffer generations remain authoritative; physical buffer release and completion waits stay unchanged.
acceptance: Use the existing unchanged-generation contract, independent CPU oracle and eight-process balanced uninstrumented cohorts. Require complete-generation and first-token controls, initial/resident tail bounds, host RSS bounds, mapping/command/rendering regressions and unrelated ONNX execution. Compare against repaired Doe for incremental admission and Dawn separately; this cannot establish the incumbent ambition unless independently met. Retain failures without outcome-selected reruns.
ownership: The live allocation registry and generations invalidate descriptors. Destroy waits for submitted work and physically releases the buffer as before. Retired descriptor metadata/pools survive until the next descriptor preparation or runtime teardown, with no new allocations, no buffer reuse changes and no growth beyond already owned descriptor state.
